{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|The Espos were brutal in their interrogation of prisoners, seeking the ringleaders. It was the first time I had seen anyone use The Burning [&hellip;] I will not leave my mate in the hands of the kind of people who would do that.|[[Atuarre]] to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Han Solo at Stars' End">''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]''</ref>}}
'''The Burning''' was the name given to a form of [[Torture/Legends|torture]] that consisted of the repeated use of a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], set at a low power level, to slowly sear the flesh of an individual's body down to the bone. It was common practice for an interrogator using this method to begin with one of the victim's legs so as to immobilize them. The interrogator would repeat the process with other parts of the victim's body until the victim gave the interrogator the answers he or she wanted, until the victim perished, or the torturer satisfied.

==History==
In cases in which a victim possessed knowledge that an interrogator desired, the Burning was an extremely effective means of obtaining information. Forcing an individual to watch as another was subjected to this particularly brutal torture method also proved to be effective. However, when a victim did not have information that an interrogator wanted, the interrogator ran the risk of eventually killing the victim.

During the [[Pius Dea Era]], the Burning was inflicted on [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]]—along with other physical torments—as part of the Trial of the Flesh stage of the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

The [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Feskitt Bobb]], one among sundry ruthless individuals, employed the Burning during the course of his hunts. The [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority's]] [[Security Police/Legends|Security Police]] performed the technique with [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifles]] in a hunt for the leaders of an uprising against the Authority during its annexation of the [[Trianii/Legends|Trianii]] colony of [[Fibuli]]. During the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] campaign against the [[Virgillian Free Alignment/Legends|Virgillian Free Alignment]], [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] stationed aboard the [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Stormwind]]'' used this technique while questioning refugees; however, they ended up killing many refugees while gaining no useful information.<ref name="bakura">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:OwenBeruDead-MOSW.png|200px|The charred corpses of [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen]] and [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Lars]].|thumb|right]]
The Burning was first described in the pages of ''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]'', by author [[Brian Daley]]. When he was asked in an interview whether he believed that [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen]] and [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Lars]] were victims of the Burning, Daley said that the scene in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], where [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] sees the [[Lars homestead/Legends|burning homestead]] and their charred corpses "was exactly what I had in mind when I wrote those lines."<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.myuselessknowledge.com/swfa/daley.html|text="A STAR WARS Fan Interviews Brian Daley"], [http://www.myuselessknowledge.com/swfa Star Wars Fanboy Association|archivedate=20050614082704}}</ref>
